panels.title: Early career, 1900 to 1918
points: First Lord of the Admiralty; Gallipoli failure, 1915

parts.text: Strength: right about the danger from Hitler
Judgement: good judgement on Germany, poor on India

keywords.def: an experienced and respected political leader
giving in to an aggressor's demands to avoid war
the minister in charge of the economy

questions.q: Explain one reason Churchill's reputation was low in the 1930s. (2 marks)
questions.a: Gallipoli was still blamed on him (1); his views on India seemed out of date to many (1)

questions.q: Core: Make three summary cards (1900 to 1918; 1918 to 1930; 1930 to 1940) with a strength, a weakness and a judgement on each.
Extend: In the portal response box, explain why some historians criticise Churchill.
questions.a: Gallipoli; views on India and empire; Bengal famine of 1943 (next lesson)

questions.q: Stretch: Was Churchill right about appeasement? Explain.
questions.a: Yes: Hitler broke the Munich Agreement in March 1939

options: Giving in to demands to avoid war
questions.a: B) Giving in to demands to avoid war. Britain's 1930s policy gave Hitler concessions, like the Sudetenland in 1938.

questions.q: Big question: best moments or whole life?
questions.a: A balanced view using the whole record and agreed criteria
